triage.line: Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline after drone attacks; Houthis control a Red Sea island near global shipping routes.
triage.headline: Saudi pipeline shut after drone attack as Houthis expand Red Sea control

clusters.state_of_play: The Iran war's economic fallout has deepened further as Saudi Arabia shut down its critical East-West pipeline -- which carries 5% of world oil supply and serves as a key alternative export route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz -- after a drone attack launched from Iraqi territory. Iraq's government confirmed the attack originated from its soil, pledged to investigate, and said it would not retaliate, briefly pushing Brent crude to $110/barrel amid fears of widening Middle East clashes. This compounds the crisis triggered by the Houthi rebels' rapid seizure of Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline, including the port of Mocha and the strategic Perim (Mayun) island commanding the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the claiming of Zuqar island, and attacks on the Hanish islands -- more than 1,000 people have been killed or wounded and tens of thousands displaced in the fighting. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree declared Red Sea shipping safe for all vessels except Saudi ships. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has personally pressed Trump to launch direct military action against the Houthis as the advance threatens Yemen's fragile truce and Saudi Arabia itself. With both Bab el-Mandeb and now an alternative Saudi pipeline route imperiled alongside fears for the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices remain elevated, borrowing costs are rising, global markets are rattled including a six-week low on Australia's ASX, US gas prices remain at record highs, and Trump's Iran deal push is further complicated. Reports indicate Vice President Vance and Secretary Rubio have privately confronted Trump over his worst fears about the war's trajectory.
